_meta.what: The decision path per company: who owns, sponsors or vetoes a three-year sponsorship. See pipeline/intel/contacts.py for the shape and the rules.
_meta.rule: A person appears here ONLY when a real page names them in that role. If a company has no marketing officer, set no_cmo true and say so — never invent one.

companies.note: Full C-suite published on the company group team page. Marketing sits with a DACH-scoped CMO; a group-level 'Chief Marketing Officer (m/w/d)' req was also live on the company's join.com board, so the seat may be widening from DACH to group — worth re-checking before an approach.

people.name: Sophia Rödiger
people.note: The buyer for a Europe-facing FE programme. In seat since Aug 2023; profiled on 1KOMMA5°'s own magazine and speaking as CMO at HEROCON in June 2026. Ex-Daimler Mobility (digital strategy) and founder of bloXmove — automotive-adjacent, no direct motorsport tie found.

people.name: Sascha Koppe
people.note: Commercial owner across the group's country businesses.

people.name: Torben Diekmann

people.name: Philipp Schröder
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO. Was Chief Sales & Marketing Officer at Sonnen and Tesla's Germany country director — a founder who has personally run a marketing function, which matters for a brand-build pitch.

companies.note: Full commercial C-suite is public on the company's own site. AlphaSense is one of the few names in this batch with a real CMO who owns brand outright, and she has taken two companies through an IPO brand-build — the exact motive a three-year sponsorship is sold against. No separately named EMEA president was found on a company page despite a large London presence; the approach runs through Zynczak with Kolstein on the commercial side.

people.name: Heather Zynczak
people.note: The buyer, and the brief's named contact — confirmed still CMO on AlphaSense's own author page and speaking as CMO on AlphaSummit 2026 material. Appointed April 2024. Prior CMO at Domo (brand launch, $0-100m) and at Pluralsight through its IPO; before that Oracle and SAP. Brand-build-for-an-IPO is her track record, which is the argument a multi-year sponsorship has to win.

people.name: Kiva Kolstein
people.note: Carries president as well as CRO, so he is the co-signer on anything sold as pipeline rather than brand. Ex-CRO at Handshake and Chief Growth Officer at Percolate.

people.name: Jack Kokko
people.note: Founder-CEO, the cheque signer. No motorsport tie found.

companies.note: Checked ALSO's own company and blog pages (ridealso.com/pages/company) and the Rivian newsroom spin-out announcement: no marketing officer of any level is named publicly, and no CEO title is used either. The company is fronted by Chris Yu as co-founder and president, with Rivian founder RJ Scaringe as chairman of the board — so the approach is Yu direct, with Scaringe as the escalation. The brief's 'Undisclosed CEO' is right that no CEO is named, but the person to call is Yu, not a vacancy. Brand signals are live despite the absent CMO: ALSO ran its own SXSW 2026 presence and has an autonomous-delivery partnership with DoorDash, so experiential and partnership marketing is already being bought — just by the president.

people.name: Chris Yu
people.note: The operating principal and the public voice of the brand — writes the company's own founding posts, gives the interviews, presents the TM-B alongside Scaringe. Was Rivian's VP of Future Programs before the spring 2025 spin-out, so he owns product and brand together in the absence of a CMO.

people.name: RJ Scaringe
people.role: Chairman of the Board (Founder & CEO, Rivian)
people.note: Co-founder of Also and chairs its board; Rivian retains a significant minority stake. Any sponsorship of this size would be visible to him, and Rivian's own brand posture would set the tone.

companies.note: Checked Anduril's own leadership and news pages: there is no CMO. Marketing sits with Jeff Miller, hired in May 2024 as the company's FIRST marketing chief at VP level — a young function reporting into a defence company whose brand is run largely through comms and the founder. IMPORTANT CORRECTION for the brief: Palmer Luckey is the founder and public face but he is NOT the CEO — Brian Schimpf is co-founder and CEO. For a European motorsport programme the sharpest door is Richard Drake, who runs Anduril UK & Europe as a P&L.

people.name: Jeff Miller
people.note: Anduril's first-ever marketing chief (May 2024), from Cruise where he was VP marketing; before that senior director of marketing/creative at Snapchat, and PepsiCo and Ogilvy earlier. Confirmed still running Anduril marketing in 2026 — he spoke at Cannes Lions on the deliberately contrarian 'Don't work for Anduril' recruitment campaign. A consumer-brand builder inside a defence prime, and one already spending on unconventional brand work, which is the profile most likely to entertain a sponsorship. No company-owned page names him and trade press varies between VP of Marketing and CMO, so treat the exact title as reported.

people.name: Matthew Steckman
people.note: The revenue owner — Anduril has no CRO; Steckman's remit explicitly covers business performance and revenue generation alongside corporate and divisional operations.

people.name: Richard Drake
people.note: The right entry point for anything European. Runs the UK and European business, which has grown from roughly 20 people to past 100. Ex-Babcock International, where he was Chief Executive of Mission Systems and Group CTO — a British defence-industrial operator who knows what a UK visibility platform is worth.

people.name: Brian Schimpf
people.note: The actual cheque signer, not Palmer Luckey. Luckey remains founder and the company's public personality (anduril.com/founders) and would carry the brand argument, but Schimpf runs the company.

companies.note: Checked the company leadership page (antora.com/company): no CMO, VP Marketing or equivalent is listed. The nearest owner of external brand is Adam Frankel, VP Communications and Public Policy — an engineering- and policy-led company, so a sponsorship pitch runs through comms and the co-founder CCO, not a marketing department.

people.name: Adam Frankel
people.note: Closest thing to a marketing owner: holds brand, comms and policy. No CMO exists above him.

people.name: David Bierman
people.note: The real commercial decision-maker — fronts customers, utilities and financiers. Public speaker (Aspen Ideas) so used to platform appearances.

people.name: Andrew Ponec

The brief named no decision-maker for Armada — it is John Zissimos to call, Dan Wright to sign.

people.name: John Zissimos
people.note: The buyer. Named as CMO on Armada's own blog, where he hosts 'News from the Edge', the company's industry podcast — a marketing chief already investing in owned media and long-form brand storytelling, which is the disposition a three-year rights deal needs.

people.note: Commercial owner. Joined from AuditBoard where he was CRO and took ARR from $50m past $250m in four years; seven years before that at AppDynamics, also as CRO, through $50m to $500m+. Hospitality-and-pipeline arguments land with him.

people.name: Dan Wright
people.note: Founder-CEO and the cheque signer; fronts the company externally (e.g. the 'Arsenal of Democracy' appearance on Armada's own blog). No decision-maker was named in the brief — this is him.

Not confirmed on a company-owned page.

people.name: Amir Haghighat

people.name: Natalie Sunderland
people.note: The buyer, and an unusually good one: her published remit is strengthening market position, accelerating growth and 'building an iconic brand'. Over two decades in strategic marketing; came from Global Head of Marketing and Communications at BNY Mellon, where she owned global brand strategy for a sponsorship-heavy institution. Named one of Business Insider's Most Innovative CMOs for 2024.

people.name: Aman Joshi
people.note: Commercial owner. 22 years at GE across GE Aviation, GE Power, GE Capital and the Global Growth Organization, latterly global GM of GE's Aeroderivative units business — an industrial turbine executive, so the engineering-partnership framing of a power-unit-era F1 argument is native to him.

people.name: KR Sridhar
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still Founder, Chairman and CEO. Founded the company in 2001; previously director of the Space Technologies Laboratory at the University of Arizona working on Mars exploration systems. Note for timing: Simon Edwards became CFO in April 2026, so a new CFO is pricing multi-year commitments.

people.name: Miguel Milano

people.name: Alexander Rinke

people.name: Matthew Mulqueen
people.note: The de facto buyer in the absence of a CMO — owns global go-to-market, sales and customer success, and is explicitly scaling regional teams across North America, EMEA and APJ. Appointed April 2026; previously CRO at LILT AI, with earlier roles at Kong and Cresta.

people.name: Harjot Gill
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still co-founder and CEO across the company's 2026 releases (including the $143m raise at a $1.5bn valuation in August 2026). With no marketing officer, he is the brand decision himself.

companies.note: Complete and current: a CMO who also owns the partner ecosystem, and a CRO appointed to accelerate growth. Both sit on Coralogix's own about page and blog. people.name: Brian Mullen
people.note: The buyer, and his remit covers the partner ecosystem as well as global marketing strategy — which is the lever for a hospitality-and-co-marketing case. Previously CMO at InfluxData, with senior go-to-market roles at Twilio and Nexus Venture Partners.

people.name: Chetan Chaudhary
people.note: Commercial owner, announced on Coralogix's own blog and introduced by Assaraf personally — hired explicitly to accelerate growth, so he is spending against pipeline.

people.name: Ariel Assaraf
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO and co-founder (founded 2014). No motorsport tie found.

companies.note: Checked corgi.insure (including its own press-release section), the company's YC profile and its jobs board: Corgi publishes no leadership page and names no marketing or revenue officer anywhere. Its own careers listings still carry a 'Founding Head of Sales' req, which confirms the gap rather than fills it — the go-to-market function is being built from scratch at a company already valued in the billions. The named executives are the two founders plus function heads in government affairs and portfolio risk. The brief named no decision-maker; it is Nico Laqua, with Emily Yuan as the operating counterpart. Re-check before an approach: a company that tripled its valuation inside three months is exactly the kind that hires its first CMO at short notice.

people.name: Emily Yuan
people.note: The nearest thing to a commercial owner in the absence of a CRO or CMO — runs operations and does the company's external interviews. No marketing officer exists above or beside her. Title from Corgi's own YC company profile; no leadership page on corgi.insure to corroborate it.

people.name: Nico Laqua
people.note: The cheque signer and, with no CMO, the brand decision too. Quoted as founder and CEO in Corgi's own press releases; also carries CTO in some records — a technical founder running the company. Corgi went from a $160m Series B at $1.3bn (May 2026) to $2.6bn weeks later on a $106m Series B1, then an extension at $4.0bn in July 2026, so capacity is not the constraint; attention is.

Marketing runs at VP level. For a sponsorship the real path is Lochmiller and Cavness — both founders front the company publicly and Cavness holds strategy — with Gordon pricing it.

people.name: Sharieff Mansour
people.note: The senior-most marketing person found; no CMO sits above him. Previously at RelationalAI, Microsoft and Orange. Sourced only from data-broker and LinkedIn records — no Crusoe-owned page names him — so confirm the seat before using it as the entry point.

people.name: Cully Cavness
people.note: Moved to president and chief strategy officer when Gordon joined; owns long-term strategy and innovation programmes and is the founder who does most of the podcast and conference circuit — the most reachable senior door. Energy background: Petrie Partners, Recurrent Engineering.

people.name: Michael Gordon
people.role: Chief Operating Officer & Chief Financial Officer
people.note: Holds both operations and finance, so a multi-year commitment is priced by him. Came from MongoDB, where he was COO and CFO through its public-company growth — he will want the deal argued in payback, not exposure.

people.name: Chase Lochmiller
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still co-founder and CEO. Ex-Polychain Capital general partner, quant researcher at Jump Trading and GETCO; Stanford CS (AI), MIT maths and physics.

people.name: Byron Foster
people.note: Joined Dana in 2021 as SVP and Chief Commercial, Marketing and Communications Officer before moving to President, Light Vehicle Systems — the incoming CEO personally owns the marketing and commercial history, which is unusual and useful here.

people.name: R. Bruce McDonald
people.note: Chairman and CEO since 2024; stays on as Chairman after the July 2026 handover.

people.name: Rick Schultz
people.note: Brief's named contact and correct: CMO since 2017, still in seat in 2026. Owns product marketing, demand gen, brand and creative, global comms, events and field marketing — a sponsorship lands squarely in his budget. Ex-SVP Marketing at Alteryx, ex-Oracle.

people.name: Ron Gabrisko
people.note: Worldwide sales and go-to-market; the co-signer on anything pitched as pipeline rather than brand.

people.name: Samuel Bonamigo
people.note: Runs EMEA and was still referenced in that role in the Sep 2025 Benelux/Nordics appointment release — the regional budget holder for European race weekends.

people.name: Ali Ghodsi
people.note: Cheque signer at the top of a company of this size; realistically a ratifier, not the entry point.

companies.note: No CMO exists, but this is the one company in the batch where that does not matter: marketing and communications for Divergent sit with George Biggs, who spent nearly 13 years at McLaren Automotive and left as its Chief Sales & Marketing Officer. DEEP MOTORSPORT AND PERFORMANCE-AUTOMOTIVE TIES throughout — Divergent's DAPS platform supplies 3D-printed structural parts to McLaren (a multi-year partnership; the W1's titanium front suspension mirrors an F1 pushrod layout with inboard dampers), Bugatti (Tourbillon chassis and suspension), Aston Martin and Mercedes-AMG, and the group's own Czinger Vehicles builds record-setting hypercars. This is a company that already sells into the racing supply chain; a sponsorship conversation here is a supplier conversation, not a halo one. The two Czingers are confirmed on Divergent's own company pages; Biggs is not named there, so his seat is reported from motorsport trade press and confirm the title before an approach. Divergent has also built a large aerospace-and-defence business (Saab fuselages, GA-ASI flight hardware, a Palantir partnership, USAF EWAAC) under a dedicated chief strategy officer for A&D — relevant only as evidence that the group runs several brand identities at once and is used to buying credibility in adjacent industries.

people.name: George Biggs
people.role: Chief Communications Officer, Divergent Technologies (Chief Commercial Officer, Czinger Vehicles)
people.note: THE call. Owns marketing and communications for Divergent while serving as CCO of Czinger Vehicles (appointed May 2025). Ex-McLaren Automotive Chief Sales & Marketing Officer and managing director for Asia-Pacific across nearly 13 years — he has sat on the manufacturer side of the McLaren brand and knows exactly what motorsport rights are worth and what they cost. The warmest leadership tie in this batch.

people.name: Kevin Czinger
people.note: Founder and the inventor behind DAPS, named and quoted on Divergent's own company pages; also CEO of Czinger Vehicles, the hypercar marque. The performance-brand instinct in the group is his — he built a car company to prove the manufacturing platform, which is the same logic that makes a racing programme legible to him.

people.name: Lukas Czinger
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still co-founder and chief executive on Divergent's own company pages and in the LA500 2026 listing. Note the title has moved — earlier company announcements (2024) carry him as President & COO, current ones as President & CEO. Runs the end-to-end AI-design, additive-manufacturing and robotic-assembly platform and fronts the technology story publicly.

companies.note: Checked Eaton's corporate-officers listing and its 2025-26 appointment releases: there is no group Chief Marketing Officer among the senior leadership team. Global marketing sits at director or divisional-VP level (data-broker records name Camie Hanily, Global Marketing & Communications Director, and Andrew Agan, VP Global Marketing for Crouse-Hinds/B-Line/Oil & Gas — neither confirmed on an Eaton page, so neither is listed here). A sponsorship therefore has to be bought against a division P&L, not a group marketing budget. Two live inflections shape who to call: Eaton announced on 26 Jan 2026 that it will spin off the Mobility Group (https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/mobility-group-spin-off.html), which is where the supercharger/driveline heritage sits, and the EMEA presidency changed hands on 1 Jun 2025. Motorsport: checked, no current Eaton motorsport programme or team partnership found — the motorsport adjacency is product heritage (Eaton superchargers, driveline) inside the business being separated, not a sponsorship history.

people.name: Scott Adams
people.note: Divisional P&L owner for electrification — the natural buyer of an F1-2026 / Formula E electrification story. Named 31 Jan 2026, reporting to Joao Faria, president of the Vehicle Group; came up through eMobility as SVP of product strategy, sales AND marketing, so he has personally run the marketing function this group otherwise lacks. Caveat: his division is inside the Mobility Group Eaton is spinning off, so a three-year commitment signed here may be signed by a different company by the time it runs.

people.name: Omar Zaire
people.role: President, Corporate and Electrical Sector, EMEA
people.note: The right seat for a European series: owns Eaton's corporate presence and the Electrical P&L across EMEA. In post since 1 Jun 2025, succeeding Tim Darkes; 27 years in the electrical industry, 16 of them at Eaton; reports to Heath Monesmith, COO of the Electrical Sector. A first-year regional president with a brand-building mandate is the most approachable budget in the group.

people.name: Paulo Ruiz
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO — in seat since 1 Jun 2025, after a year as president and COO. Ran the Industrial Sector (Aerospace, Vehicle, Mobility, Filtration) before that, so he knows the electrification and vehicle businesses from the inside. Electrical engineer by training. With no group CMO, an approach that reaches him has to be framed as strategy, not marketing spend.

companies.note: Checked emeraldai.co/team and emeraldai.co/company: no CMO, VP Marketing or comms lead is listed. A ~2-year-old, research-led company (founded 2024) — the sponsorship conversation is with Sivaram directly, with Padilla as the commercial operator. Do not expect a marketing budget line to exist yet.

people.name: Daniel Padilla
people.role: Chief of Staff & Director, Commercial Strategy & Operations
people.note: The commercial operator around the CEO; joined from Rondo Energy. In a company this size, the practical route to Sivaram's diary.

people.name: Dr. Varun Sivaram
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still Founder & CEO. Ex-Chief Strategy & Innovation Officer at Ørsted and ex-CTO of ReNew Power — an unusually brand-literate energy executive, and the person who would personally decide a sponsorship.

people.name: Prof. Ayse Coskun
people.note: Academic authority on orchestrating data-centre power demand for grid response — the technical counterpart if the pitch is an energy-flexibility workstream with a team's operations rather than a logo.

people.name: Kellee Khalil
people.note: The buyer. Owns business, brand and marketing strategy; with the company since inception and still named on 2026 releases. A serial entrepreneur and brand builder — the profile that responds to a sponsorship narrative rather than a media schedule.

people.name: Chloe Ke
people.role: Executive Vice President, Strategy and Sales
people.note: Nearest thing to a commercial officer — strategy and sales in one seat.

people.name: Teague Egan

people.name: Amit Patwardhan
people.note: Technical counterpart for any battery-materials or lithium-chemistry workstream with a race team.

Will Bryk is co-founder and CEO of Exa; Jeff Wang is a co-founder without a published officer title, one of three (Bryk, Dan McArdle, Jeffrey Wang) named in a16z's own investment announcement (https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-exa/). people.name: Jeff Wang
people.note: Co-founded Exa with Bryk in 2021 (they met studying CS at Harvard); ex-Plaid. Named as co-founder in the funding coverage and on his own company email address, but no CEO, COO or president title is published for him — the brief's 'CEO & Co-founder' is wrong. Still worth knowing as the second founder in the room.

people.name: Will Bryk
people.note: The actual decision-maker and the only realistic buyer at this stage — a founder-led company with no marketing officer. Harvard CS; early engineer at Cresta. Fronts the company publicly (AI Engineer speaker circuit) and posts Exa's scale numbers himself (80bn pages served, 1.4tn URLs tracked, Aug 2026), so he owns the brand narrative personally.

companies.note: Checked the management team page on Fervo's investor site (now NASDAQ: FRVO): no CMO or VP Marketing is listed. people.name: Sarah Jewett

people.name: Dawn Owens
people.role: SVP, Head of Development & Commercial Markets
people.note: Owns development and commercial markets since 2020; the counterpart if the pitch is framed around customer and offtake audiences.

people.name: Tim Latimer
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO and a director since 2018. Now runs a listed company, so a sponsorship needs a stated commercial rationale, not a founder's enthusiasm.

people.name: Lin Qiao
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO and co-founder. Led PyTorch at Meta before founding Fireworks. people.name: Dmytro Dzhulgakov

No David Burt appears anywhere in Firmus Technologies' leadership; the company is run by co-CEOs Oliver Curtis and Tim Rosenfield, who founded it (with Jonathan Levi).
